tldr: Deliverables complete: research doc 11-ux-fa.md (~5.5k words, Persian summary first), ux-spec.md (~7k words: 18 customer screens C01-C18, 17 admin screens A01-A17 incl. demo sim, state tables, payment-mismatch matrix, RBAC matrix, Mini App rules, 45-event notification matrix, acceptance checklist), data/copy.fa.json with 1,370 flat keys (249 shared web snapshot + 1,121 new, 139 notification templates, 10 SMS), design-tokens.json with light/dark (50 contrast pairs, 0 failures).

This run found earlier partial work in the repo (tokens, copy parts, scripts). I fixed the copy linter, which flagged Persian digits as ASCII (Python \d matches Unicode), added an OVERRIDE mechanism, and brought the build to 0 errors. Three non-compliant web-snapshot strings (quote.lockHint, quote.savingsNote, system.ratesHaltedBody) and the OTP SMS (now 1 segment) are overridden in the JSON; the web owner should adopt them.

Search budget: only 5 searches plus one blocked fetch (core.telegram.org EGRESS_BLOCKED). Trust and pain-point findings are repo evidence from specialists 01/03/04/07 plus labelled hypotheses H1-H8 with verify_how. Overall confidence is low for user-behaviour claims. Design system and copy are machine-checked.

Pricing flag: the illustrative USD 100 new-card price with placeholder defaults is 32,103,000 IRT, +24.9% over the USDT reference, versus competitor fees of 4-6%. The UI therefore keeps 'savings vs market' hidden unless fresh sourced data exists and legal review is done; specialist 12 must calibrate.

Honest-conversion rules, rush/express UX (30-minute lock, fast +4% min 100k IRT SLA 30 min 20/h, express +10% min 300k IRT SLA 10 min 6/h, auto refund of rush fee on SLA miss) and a performance budget (<=170 KB gz JS, <=350 KB first load, LCP<=2.5 s slow-4G) are specified. The budget is an assumption to be measured.

The UX wish for 'savings vs market' conflicts with the legal caution on comparative claims, and with the example price being 24.9% over reference against competitors' 4-6%.
